learning: If the oval holds at 20/20 and the bends gain progress, the footprint is a useful lever and can be combined with a modest spread change. If the oval drops, or the s-bend and slalom stay at max_error near 0.06, the bend limit is probably controller-side (gains or base speed), and the baseline 12 mm footprint remains the reference.
notes: Complete package for the 16 mm footprint test. Geometry matches the Builder's proposal exactly, and the controller is the iteration-0 baseline unchanged so the footprint is the only variable. Based on the same race history as the Builder's feedback, with no controller compensation required.
rationale: The Builder's proposal is a single-variable test against the iteration-0 baseline: the sensor footprint rises from 12 mm to 16 mm, and every other geometry value stays the same. Iteration 0 is still the best design (356.6): it finishes the oval 20/20 in about 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15, but leaves the track on the s-bend (progress 0.17) and slalom (progress 0.12) at max_error near 0.061 m. Every other geometry change has hurt. Moving the row to y=0.07 or y=0.03 collapsed the oval to 0/20 (iterations 3 and 4), so y=0.05 is a sharp optimum. The 8 mm footprint (iteration 5) also collapsed the oval to 0/20. The 16 mm footprint is the last sensing-resolution lever the Builder has not yet tested. At a 12 mm pitch, 16 mm footprints overlap, so the summed reading should stay above the 0.05 line-loss threshold and the signal should be smoother than at 8 mm. I therefore keep the iteration-0 controller exactly (kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2], last_direction). Changing the controller at the same time would confound the footprint test, and the Builder has asked for a clean comparison. The signal scale depends only on the weights and the reading-weighted average, so the larger footprint needs no new weights. I expect the oval to stay near 20/20 at about 1.65 s, with bend progress possibly rising above 0.17 and 0.12. This is untested. Measurements cover all of the Builder's requested signals plus controller_errors and noise_robustness.
